## Why This Is Asked

This question probes understanding of tokenization, attention, and how vocabulary updates impact model behavior in production-like settings.

## Key Concepts

- Tokenization boundaries and subword vs whole-token attention
- Attention distribution diagnostics (KL divergence, entropy)
- Lightweight dynamic vocabulary fallback without retraining

## Code Example

```python
# toy: compare two attention maps and print KL difference
import numpy as np
def kl(p, q):
    p = np.asarray(p, dtype=float)
    q = np.asarray(q, dtype=float)
    p = p / p.sum()
    q = q / q.sum()
    return float(np.sum(p * np.log(p / (q + 1e-9))))
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend metrics to multilingual vocabularies?
- How would you guard against adversarial token proposals?

## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses the ability to build a privacy-conscious, low-latency retrieval system with real-world enterprise constraints.

## Key Concepts
- Tenancy-aware ACLs enforced at the passage level
- Adaptive chunking guided by query intent and token budget
- Latency budgeting, caching strategies, and retry semantics
- Embedding model selection and vector index design
- Observability and testing for correctness guarantees

## Code Example
```javascript
// Adaptive chunking based on query intent
async function chunkDocument(doc, query, maxTokens = 256) {
  const intent = await detectQueryIntent(query);
  const boundaries = intent === 'exact'
    ? splitBySentence(doc)
    : intent === 'overview'
      ? splitBySection(doc)
      : splitByParagraph(doc);

  return boundaries
    .map(b => ({ text: b, tokens: countTokens(b) }))
    .filter(b => b.tokens <= maxTokens)
    .map(b => ({ ...b, embedding: await embed(b.text) }));
}
```
